goal: log-notify v0.1: Rust daemon that tails configured log files, matches per-source regexes, and emits freedesktop notifications through D-Bus with reliable bounded delivery.
active_goals: T1-T13 complete; T14 release workflow implemented and local static package verified.
v0.1 code is complete and CI is green. Only the first release tag/publish remains.
Awaiting approval to create tag v0.1.0 and publish the GitHub release.
decisions: Rust stable, edition 2024, single binary, Linux only, synchronous main loop, inotify-driven with no polling.
Read logs only; no native tool hooks; no replay or persistence; every source starts at end of file.
Default config is data: sources, patterns, templates, urgency, cooldown, and queue capacity are TOML. No tool-specific code.
TOML config with serde; compile every regex at startup; fail loud with file, line, and reason.
Missing log source at startup: warn, watch nearest existing ancestor directory, continue. Re-resolve when intermediate directories appear. Permission denied is fatal.
Main loop never calls D-Bus. Dedicated notifier worker with a bounded per-source queue: default 10, range 1..=100.
Queue overflow drops the oldest event of that source and logs it. No durable spool; pending events are lost on restart.
Notification failures retry 3 times with 1/2/4 s backoff and a 5 s zbus method timeout; missing service or exhausted retries drop and log.
Dropped-event log defaults to /var/log/log-notify.log; if unwritable, warn once and fall back to stderr.
zbus 6.5 async API driven by zbus::block_on in the worker; no async runtime.
Non-UTF-8 lines use lossy conversion. Over-cap lines keep the capped prefix, discard the rest, and match once.
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unset: use /run/user/<uid> if present, else exit with a clear error.
--once exits after the first regex match is processed; normal mode waits for delivery or drop outcome. Config paths: /etc/log-notify/log-notify.toml, then ~/.config/log-notify/log-notify.toml.
License ISC, copyright skea999.
SIGHUP config reload deferred to v0.2; v0.1 requires restart.

CI adapted from Ursine: one containerized verify job, Alpine image, clippy-driven test gate, static/SAST/deps/duplicates/SBOM/docs gates, tag-driven static-musl release. No Ursine Nix/GUI/installer jobs.
Host toolchain is not used: every gate runs in the container through scripts/dev.sh or GitHub Actions.
Rust scaffold uses edition 2024 and the direct inotify 0.11.x crate; daemon behavior is not implemented yet.
Config uses serde + toml 1.x with Spanned fields; semantic errors report file, line, column, reason.
Config defaults: line_cap_bytes 8192, dropped_log /var/log/log-notify.log, queue_capacity 10, urgency normal, cooldown 0, enabled true.
Explicit --config path bypasses default resolution; otherwise /etc/log-notify/log-notify.toml then ~/.config/log-notify/log-notify.toml.
Patterns compile once at config load; Source keeps the raw strings for diagnostics and a CompiledPattern for matching.
Templates support {line} and named capture groups; {{ and }} are literal braces; unknown placeholders, unmatched braces, and a capture named line are config errors.
No match path avoids template rendering and notification allocation.
Tailer opens at EOF, tracks dev/inode/offset, buffers partial lines, keeps a capped prefix, discards the rest until newline, and marks truncated lines.
Invalid UTF-8 is converted with String::from_utf8_lossy per line; no panic.
Read/open errors carry the source path in TailError; the event loop will isolate failures per source.
Watch the nearest existing ancestor directory, not the source file; reconcile every source on events. This covers missing files and rotation uniformly.
Use inotify nonblocking reads with rustix poll and a nonblocking self-pipe for shutdown; no polling loop.
Store dev/inode/offset in Tailer; shrink resets to byte 0, inode replacement reopens at EOF, delete/recreate opens at EOF.
Watcher warnings (missing source, failed watch, rotation, overflow, read errors) are accumulated for T10 to log.
Cooldown records emission at enqueue; window boundary is inclusive (last + window allows). Tests inject Instant.
Notification delivery uses a bounded EventQueue with per-source capacities; overflow drops the oldest event of that source and logs queue_full.
Worker owns the notifier; retries transient failures 3 times with 1/2/4s, drops no_service immediately, logs terminal notify_failed.
DroppedLog appends timestamp/path/reason/detail/summary/body, flushes each line, falls back to stderr.
ZbusNotifier uses zbus 6.5 Builder::session().method_timeout(5s), block_on, urgency hint, critical expiry 0, normal/low -1; reconnects lazily after errors.
CLI uses clap; disabled sources are filtered and active indices map back to config sources.
--once uses direct delivery with retry so the process waits for the delivery/drop outcome; continuous mode uses the queue and worker.
Watcher warnings are printed to stderr; --verbose prefixes them as tail-debug lines.
Dropped log is opened at startup with stderr fallback; dry-run still computes matches and cooldown but never touches D-Bus.
Lock uses rustix flock nonblocking exclusive; the open File is held for the process lifetime.
signal-hook iterator thread calls Watcher shutdown handle on SIGTERM/SIGINT; SIGHUP is logged and ignored.
Watcher poll treats EINTR as a wake and retries, so signal interruption does not fail shutdown.
Fixture integration loads the shipped config and matches fail2ban, clamav, tracee, aide, auditd sample lines.
Source behavior stays config-only; the only hardcoded log path in Rust is the dropped-event log default.
risks: Watcher warnings are not yet printed by a CLI; T10 must consume them.
Queue overflow or permanent notification-service absence drops events; every drop is logged, but delivery is not guaranteed.
Pending in-memory events are lost on restart by design.
A retry after an uncertain reply can duplicate a notification. Accepted: duplicate over silent loss.
Session-memory scripts fail on this host with Nix libc relocation errors; context-mode ctx_* tools and this state file are the working alternative.
